full_text:
Ali Nur al-Din, an affluent young merchant of Cairo, was ruined by dishonest partners and reduced to sailing aboard an Alexandrian merchant vessel. In a foreign port, he met Miriam, a brilliant maiden who had been captured by pirates, renowned for her extraordinary skill in embroidery, navigation, and mathematics.

Recognizing each other’s noble character, they escaped their oppressors aboard a swift caravel, with Miriam serving as the navigator, reading the stars and charting courses with masterly skill.

When foreign corsairs pursued their ship across the Mediterranean, Miriam and Ali worked as a united team: while Ali commanded the defense at the prow, Miriam steered the vessel through dangerous rocky shoals where the heavier pirate ships ran aground!

Reaching the friendly port of Alexandria, they established a grand maritime emporium, using Miriam’s nautical charts and Ali’s commercial honesty to build a thriving merchant fleet that connected Egypt, Syria, and Andalusia in peaceful trade.

Their union became a celebrated legend of maritime partnership, demonstrating that mutual courage, intellect, and teamwork are more powerful than all the fleets of tyrants.
moral: Courageous resourcefulness, nautical skill, and mutual fidelity triumph over foreign captivity.
